headline.purpose: The selected part's name at the top of Details.

title.purpose: View headings: power tree loads, firmware, work tabs, the design panel.

title-small.purpose: Parts list heading, card and block titles, guide steps.

body.purpose: All interface text and chat. Long text caps at 62 to 72ch.

body-small.purpose: Secondary text, hints, table headers, chips.

label.purpose: The short view names under rail icons.

data.purpose: Every measured or counted value: designators, V, A, W, mm, quantities, percentages. Tabular figures.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: The only shadow: floating tool tray, design bar, live-build note, view cube, export menu, and the parts tray when it floats below 860px.

shadows.name: cursor
shadows.purpose: Filter on live-build agent cursors so they read over any part.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for state changes, entrances and presses.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons, chips, rail buttons, icon buttons and view-cube buttons give way on press; colour transitions share the 120ms.

motion.name: view-in
motion.purpose: A view arriving after a rail switch. Chat messages use the same at 240ms.

motion.name: tray-in-up
motion.purpose: The floating tool tray, design bar and live note rising into place.

motion.name: pop-in
motion.value: 140ms ease-out; scale 0.97 and -4px, origin top right

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: Right-panel content swapping between Agent, Details and the tool tab.

motion.name: explode
motion.purpose: The model explodes when a teardown opens, and on Play.

motion.name: grow-in
motion.purpose: Parts growing in during the live build.

motion.name: skeleton
motion.purpose: First load of a lazily loaded view.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: CSS transitions and animations collapse to their end state; the viewer drops the flow dots and auto-rotate; the cursor click ring is hidden; the opening explode jumps to its end state.

components.description: Default graphite button, 32px high; used for most actions.

narrative.overview:
Teardown Lab is a dark professional tool in the family of Flux and Figma. The exploded 3D model is the workspace: the stage runs edge to edge between a narrow icon rail on the left and a slim panel on the right, and every piece of chrome is a lifted shade of the same cool blue-black graphite. The interface recedes so the product, its parts and its wiring carry the colour.

The system is dense and quiet. Text is warm off-white on graphite, panels are separated by hairlines rather than boxes, and the only controls that sit on top of the model live in one floating tray docked bottom-centre. Hue is rationed: amber says "selected", the wire-kind colours say what a connection carries, and coral, red and green report check results. Everything else is graphite and ink.

Motion is short and answers a change of state: a view rises 4 px as it arrives, trays slide in from their own edge, presses give way to 97%. The one long motion is the model exploding when a teardown opens. Under reduced motion the interface transitions, the flowing wire dots, auto-rotate and the live-build grow-in all drop to their end state.
keyCharacteristics: A graphite ladder of seven surfaces, the 3D stage the deepest and floating trays and hovers the most raised.
The 3D model fills the space between the rail and the right panel; no boxed preview.
One floating tool tray per 3D view, the signature move.
Geist Sans for the interface, Geist Mono with tabular figures for every measured value.
Amber is selection only; in the chrome the wire-kind and check-state colours are the only other hues.
One soft shadow, for things that float.

rules.name: The Amber Means Selected Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the selected part, its label, its row, its node and its card, and nothing else. Focus rings are ink, warnings are coral, never amber.

rules.name: The Wire Kind Rule
rules.body: A connection's colour is its kind. Every view that draws a connection takes its colour from the one `KIND_COLOR` map, and every colour is repeated in words beside it (chip label, legend, table cell).

rules.name: The Graphite Ladder Rule
rules.body: Depth is a lightness step on the same hue, never a new colour: stage, sunk, paper, panel, tray, raised, hover, from deepest to most raised.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Data Rule
rules.body: Every measured or counted value (V, A, W, mm, U7, x2, 85%) is set in Geist Mono with tabular figures. Words around it stay in Geist Sans.

rules.name: The One Display Rule
rules.body: There is one display size and it lives on the start screen. Inside the workspace the largest text is the part name in Details.

rules.name: The Only Floaters Cast Rule
rules.body: A surface gets the Float shadow only when it sits on top of the model or another region. Panels, cards and rows separate with hairlines and graphite steps.

dos: **Do** let the 3D stage fill the space between the rail and the right panel, on `stage` (oklch(15.5% 0.012 256)).
**Do** take every surface from the graphite ladder and separate regions with 1 px `rule` hairlines.
**Do** set every measured or counted value in Geist Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** colour a connection by its kind from `KIND_COLOR` and name the kind in words beside it.
**Do** mark every part and connection observed, inferred or assumed with the full, half or empty disc and its word.
**Do** put on-model controls in the one floating tray, bottom-centre, with the Float shadow.
**Do** keep interface motion at 300 ms or less and tied to a change of state; the model's 1.3 s explode is the one long motion. Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** use amber for anything but selection: not for focus, warnings, highlights or brand.

**Don't** add hues to the chrome beyond selection, the wire kinds and the check states. Hues that encode data on the model (part colours, fit classes, board copper, agent cursors) stay on the model and are named in a legend.
**Don't** box the 3D model in a card or frame it as a preview inside a page.
**Don't** give resting panels, cards or rows a shadow.
**Don't** set numbers in the sans face, or words in the mono face.
**Don't** dress an estimate as a measurement: an inferred or assumed value keeps its confidence mark.
